source_material: Owner screenshot: complete Leptochloa dubia p.226 treatment. Previous key fragment and following L. virgata treatment excluded. No scans/figures republished.

option.label: Firm perennial base
option.detail: Confirm the crown/base is firm. Gould does not call it knotty or equate firmness with underground rhizomes.

option.label: No stolons or rhizomes
option.detail: Gould explicitly describes this species without either organ. Verify the attached crown, underground stems and surface stems; an unexamined structure is unknown, not absent.

option.label: One nearly sessile spikelet per branch node
option.detail: Inspect attachment at one flowering-branch node. Gould describes solitary, subsessile spikelets; do not count florets inside a spikelet as separate spikelets.

option.label: Hidden closed-flowering spikelets in lower sheaths
option.detail: Inspect lower sheath axils for separate perfect cleistogamous spikelets. Closed flowers on the same plant are not a second species or a normal exposed terminal branch.

option.label: Lance-shaped outer glumes, awnless
option.detail: Locate both OUTER glumes. Gould describes them as lanceolate and awnless; second usually 4–5 mm, first slightly shorter. This is separate from lemma awn evidence.

option.label: Lemma rounded on back, blunt and usually notched
option.detail: Inspect an INNER lemma: broad, rounded on back, truncate and usually notched at apex. A notch is not evidence of an awn, glume keel or gland pit.

option.label: Fine short hairs on lemma margins
option.detail: Gould permits a hairless lemma OR fine marginal puberulence. Do not require a conspicuous hair tuft or transfer these hairs to a glume.

evidence.note: Blades mostly 2–6(–8) mm wide; preserve usual and parenthetical endpoints. Width bands overlap at their boundaries.

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Confirm the firm base and actual stem organs
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould explicitly describes a tufted perennial with a firm base but without stolons or rhizomes. Confirm any claimed runner is a connected stem rather than a root or lower flowering culm.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: A verified stolon or rhizome conflicts with this primary account. An unexamined underground structure remains unknown.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Explicit Gould p.226 absence, not inference from tufting or source silence.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Leptochloa dubia, printed p.226

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Separate a true lemma awn from a tiny point or notch
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould describes lanceolate awnless glumes and broad blunt/notched lemmas. Diggs explicitly says both glumes and lemmas are awnless. A verified true lemma awn conflicts; a minute tip, notch or uncertain beginner short-bristle observation does not.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: Use the attached inner lemma. Do not infer an awn from a sharp glume, grass branch or a different plant.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Exact Diggs text p.1282; tiny supplementary mucronate reports are not treated as true awns.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Leptochloa dubia, printed p.226

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Inspect separate lower-sheath spikelets and count florets
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould reports solitary nearly sessile spikelets on the branches, usually 3–8 florets with occasional 2, plus regularly produced perfect cleistogamous spikelets hidden in lower sheath axils. Lower sterile-shoot sheaths can be compressed/keeled and pilose.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: These hidden closed flowers are on the same species. Drying-induced leaf roll, lower-sheath hairs and membrane versus cilia measurements retain their own context.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Gould p.226; next Leptochloa virgata entry excluded; no new voucher certification.
